_meta.indication: Treatment of patients 18 years and older with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including pyelonephritis caused by designated susceptible bacteria (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterobacter cloacae species complex).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy noninferiority (NI) trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to meropenem-vaborbactam (2 g/2 g) IV over 3 hours every 8 hours or piperacillin-tazobactam.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years and older with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including acute pyelonephritis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint (per protocol): overall success (composite of clinical success and microbiological eradication) at the end of intravenous therapy (EOIVT) visit; an important secondary endpoint was overall success at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit Day 15-19.
pivotal_trials.n: 550 subjects randomized (274 meropenem-vaborbactam, 276 piperacillin-tazobactam); 545 received at least one dose (272 and 273).
pivotal_trials.result: At EOIVT (m-MITT), overall success 183/186 (98.4%) meropenem-vaborbactam vs 165/175 (94.3%) piperacillin-tazobactam; treatment difference 4.1% (95% CI 0.3%, 8.8%) — meropenem-vaborbactam demonstrated superiority. At TOC, 124/162 (76.5%) vs 112/153 (73.2%); difference 3.3% (95% CI -6.2%, 13.0%) — noninferior.

key_safety: Most frequently reported adverse reactions (≥3%) were headache (8.8% vs 4.4% piperacillin/tazobactam), phlebitis/infusion site reactions (4.4% vs 0.7%), and diarrhea (3.3% vs 4.4%). Treatment was discontinued due to adverse reactions in 2.9% (8/272) of VABOMERE patients vs 5.1% (14/273). Key warnings include hypersensitivity reactions, seizure potential, C. difficile-associated diarrhea, and thrombocytopenia.
target_moa: Meropenem is a penem antibacterial that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); vaborbactam is a cyclic boronic acid beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects meropenem from degradation by certain serine beta-lactamases such as Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC), and has no antibacterial activity of its own.
modality: Small molecule combination product: a penem antibacterial (meropenem) plus a cyclic boronic acid beta-lactamase inhibitor (vaborbactam).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

summary.text: VABOMERE was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA relying in part on prior findings for meropenem (Merrem, NDA 050706). It was granted QIDP designation in December 2013, fast track designation in March 2016, and priority review; approval was supported by a single adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 cUTI trial (Study 505). It was not an accelerated approval and was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The NDA was submitted under Section 505(b)(2) of the Food Drug and Cosmetic Act and relies in part on the Agency's prior findings of safety and effectiveness of meropenem.

In this NDA, submitted under Section 505(b)(2) of the Food Drug and Cosmetic Act, the Applicant is seeking the indication of cUTI including pyelonephritis. The Applicant is relying in part on the Agency's previous findings of safety and effectiveness of the listed drug, Merrem (meropenem for injection), NDA 050706.
Meropenem-vaborbactam was granted a qualified infectious disease product (QIDP) designation in December 2013 and fast track designation in March 2016 and this NDA was granted a priority review.
A single successful adequate and well-controlled clinical trial in cUTI was considered to be acceptable to support the cUTI indication.
